text.content:
Since the First City, vampires known as princes have ruled over their kind. Princes do not rule for altruistic reasons - they do so to feed their own need to dominate others and to provide for their own security. There is no democracy, only the strong who rule as prince. The titles and duties of the office have changed as civilizations changed; a "prince" may be known as "king," "duke," "archbishop" and others borrowed from human history, and women rule as prince just as often, known variously as "queen" or "duchess."

It is traditionally the eldest Cainite who rules, his age conferring the honor. In the Dark Medieval, though, age does not necessarily translate into power, and only the strong rule. In the War of Princes, many younger vampires are seizing domains from complacent elders, and the elders are choosing to either bequeath their titles to the young in hopes of hiding in the shadows, or defend their domains with talon and fist.

Predators are territorial, and domains mean power. Without domain, a prince is not a prince. Domain may mean a university town in England or a stretch of plains in central Europe ruled from a stronghold - the larger the domain, the more power and influence the prince holds. Usually a prince rules a city and claims domain over everything within it, which forces other Cainites to acquiesce to his rule by fealty or brute force.

Rights and Responsibilities of a Prince

There is no universal code of princely conduct; aside from the Old Ways, a prince may govern as she sees fit. Still, a prince is measured by the power and influence she wields over her subjects. Princedom grants a prince certain rights and privileges, but it also demands that certain expectations and duties be followed - princes who ignore their responsibilities often find themselves without support.

  • Destruction - Only a prince may destroy (or order the destruction of) another vampire. The power of Final Death over vassals is the ultimate proof of a prince's claim.
  • Siring - Only a prince may sire freely; other vampires must gain her permission. Those who disobey are destroyed along with their childer.
  • Domain - Any vampire in a prince's domain becomes her vassal. The prince may bequeath domain as a reward or offer it as a bribe.
  • Feeding - The prince establishes feeding grounds and any rules governing feeding.
  • Upholding the Old Ways - The Traditions grant a prince the charter to rule, but only if she upholds the Traditions; only the complacent rule through sheer force alone.
  • Protection - The prince must be ready to defend her subjects at any time. A prince who does nothing when a vassal is destroyed by a rival or another vassal risks losing her credibility.
  • Shepherding the flock - The prince must make sure there are enough humans to sustain her vassals, setting hunting limits and feeding grounds while also making sure the mortal flock remains healthy, lest her vassals turn on each other from hunger.

The Officers of the Court

No prince rules completely alone. No single vampire could enforce her will across a vast domain without vassals to act as her hands and eyes. Wise princes court influential, talented Cainites when making their bids for power, creating a cabinet of advisors to assist in handling some or all of the duties of a fiefdom. The following posts are most often seen at courts:

  • Sheriff - Handles matters of security and jurisdiction, keeping neonates from causing too much hell and keeping unwanted visitors out. In wartime, sheriffs may become sergeants for the warmaster, assisting in coordinating the city's defenses when the prince and warmaster are on the battlefield.
  • Warmaster - General of the prince's army, for any prince who can muster enough forces to be called an army. If the sheriff is concerned with city security, the warmaster is concerned with the domain as a whole.
  • Seneschal - The prince's right hand, occupied with the dry business of governance. It is she who chooses (with the right bribe, occasionally) which complaints will go before the prince. In some domains seneschals are mere lackeys; in others they wield considerable power and are perhaps the true power behind the throne.
  • Keeper - The prince's spiritual advisor and counselor. Some still use older @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZJx9H3XnU8yQGy9s]{Malkavian} and @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu} oracles, but most call upon ashen priests, the teachers and leaders of one of the Roads of enlightenment. Keepers advise their princes on matters political and mystical and may lead sacraments of the Roads.
  • Chamberlain - The social heart of the prince's court, organizing feasts and tourneys and welcoming visiting dignitaries. She is also a skilled gossip and rumormonger, able to take the pulse of the subjects and discover detractors.
  • Scourge - Acts as the prince's private executioner, patrolling the domain for unwanted visitors - @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.SNuXttNqxzJ6uPXv]{Caitiff}, Autarkis and other undesirables - and either bringing them to the prince or destroying them outright. The scourge need not worry about the political ramifications of her acts or the sniping of a prince's critics as the sheriff often must; the post is not one to encourage friendly relationships, and many Cainites fear and distrust the scourge.

pages.name: Feudal Lextalionis: Ranks of the Kingdoms of Night

text.content:
Cainite society has found its fullest feudal flowering in what vampires call Feudal Lextalionis - the system at the heart of the War of Princes. It is tied closely to the Road of Kings, which concerns itself with the proper distribution and maintenance of authority, though not every ruler follows the Road of Kings; most at least pay lip service to it with the help of knowledgeable advisors. Unlike mortal nobility, gender is no barrier to power in Cainite feudalism - men and women alike fill every rank.

While the High Clans enjoy many benefits of Feudal Lextalionis, the Low Clans are not so fortunate, and rarely receive the same treatment routinely given to High Clans. It is possible for a Low Clan vampire to rise in the ranks, but she must work twice as hard and endure suspicion and second-guessing from her superiors; low-blooded Cainites are more likely to receive a posting at court that carries no noble rank. Still, the War of Princes has begun to blur the lines between High and Low Clans, and some low-blooded vampires have distinguished themselves on the battlefield, winning title and domain for themselves.

Ranks

  • Monarchs - The regents of Cainite kingdoms spanning across Europe and into Outremer. Most are Methuselahs and were once lords who grew powerful in the years between Rome's fall and the end of the Long Night. In the War of Princes, monarchs goad lords and princes into battle, seeking to expand their domains and secure their uncertain futures. Some monarchs prefer to rule in secret, while others are not shy about appearing, the better to inspire their lords.
  • Lords/Ladies - Command vast armies of princes, barons and knights, ruling territories along borders similar to medieval kingdoms. Most hold their own courts once or twice a year, spending the rest of their time traveling to their vassals' courts, settling disputes, and attending ceremonies.
  • Princes - A generic title for any vampire with domain over a significantly large and strategically valuable territory tied to the feudal system. Princes who ruled fiefdoms before the First Crusade are called counts or dukes to distinguish them from the younger princes of these nights.
  • Barons/Baronesses - The Cainites of action, usually the officers of princes and lords, serving as sheriffs, warmasters, chamberlains and the like - posts granted due to their talents and services. With enough good service, a baroness may eventually earn her own fiefdom and become a prince.
  • Knights - The lowest-ranked Cainites, but also some of the most important - they fill the armies of night and clash on the battlefields of the War of Princes. Many serve as spies or messengers for their lords, or may be granted small domains to test their worth. Knights are usually low-ranked vampires who have proven themselves worthy and sworn fealty to a baron or prince; knighthood puts a vampire in the chain of vassalage. Knights are the most likely to leave only their ashes on the battlefields, but have just as much opportunity to gain domains as spoils of war.

Fealty

Feudal Lextalionis is governed by a network of oaths and alliances that tie the courts of Europe to their lords and monarchs, called fealty. When one vampire acknowledges another as her superior through fealty, she makes a pledge of loyalty in return for protection and support - a chain tying the nocturnal nobility from knights to monarchs.

In swearing fealty, the vassal - knight, prince or lord - offers loyalty and support (political and military) to her liege, and vows never to attack the liege (though the War of Princes has seen this vow dropped occasionally). In return, the liege may grant the vassal a domain to rule, sized according to rank - knights are given taverns or neighborhoods, while barons may rule larger estates or guilds. The liege also vows to protect the vassal in court and on the battlefield. The Traditions of Caine cement the rule of the liege, allowing her to protect and offer domain and gifts to her vassals, as well as giving her authority to punish transgressions. Many princes require that a tithe be paid as part of fealty, such as a percentage of the income a domain generates, or the raising of an army of ghouls or vampires in time of war.

Princes are vassals to lords or monarchs, but the fealty is not as strict. Princes often hold fiefdoms bequeathed to them, or pay enough tithe to prevent their lord from invading them. Many princes ally themselves with a lord to present a united front against a mutual enemy, and rivals consider very carefully before starting a war with a prince allied to a lord or monarch.

pages.name: The High Clans and Low Clans

text.content:
The High Clans reign supreme in the night, being the most likely to hold noble rank and the office of prince. They believe their progenitors were the first Embraced, and that the deeds of the Low Clans in Enoch created strife and eventual destruction. In the Dark Medieval, six clans have embraced the feudal system: @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah}, Cappadocian, @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.phgt6OMwTAoAaKfR]{Lasombra}, @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador}, @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce} and @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue}.

The Low Clans are despised by the High Clans, either for their foreign ways (such as the Assamites and @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos}) or for the depths of their bloodlines' curses, which make socializing almost impossible (Malkavians and @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu}). The Low Clans comprise the Assamites, @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ssX4b2JFXF2uegC3]{Followers of Set}, @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.zCWdD1NpOCn03CwE]{Gangrel}, Malkavians, @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu}, @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} and @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere}. Despite being shut out of the ranks of the proud High Clans, the Low Clans have been gaining ground, being more in tune with the times than their isolationist brethren. A Low Clan vampire can rise in rank, but must work twice as hard and endure far more suspicion than a High Clan counterpart; several princes across Europe and Outremer are nonetheless Cainites of the Low Clans.

vtmlarp.source: Faith and Fire (Dark Ages Vampire), Chapter One: Introduction and Setting
